div.head: Duns 1.2
div.ab: Gif man secge, þæt man þæt trod awoh drife, ðonne mot se ðe þæt yrfe ah trod [o]ð to stæðe lædan ⁊ ðær syxa sum ungecorenra, ðe getrywe syn, ðone að syllan, þæt he mid folcrihte on þæt land sprece, swa his [orf] ðær up eode.

Si dicatur, quod uestigium illud iniuste minetur, tunc debet homo qui per uestigium sequitur ad locum ducere et ibi se sexto ungecorenra (id est non electorum), qui credibiles tamen sint, iurare, quod in recto puplico super illam terram loquatur, sicut pecunia sua super eam euenit.

Wenn jener [dortige Gutsbesitzer] erwidert, dass dieser [Kläger] rechtswidrig diese Spur verfolge, dann kann dieser Eigenthümer des Viehes [als Widerlegung] die Spur bis zum Ufer leiten und dort als einer von sechs [Eidesleistern], die [ihm zwar] nicht ernannt, [aber] vertrauenswerth seien, folgenden Eid ablegen: ‘dass er nach Volksrecht gegen jenes Landgut klage, da sein Vieh dort hinauf gegangen sei’.

If that [landowner there] replies that this [plaintiff] is following the track wrongfully, then this owner of the cattle may [in rebuttal] lead the track up to the bank and there, as one of six [oath-givers] who are not nominated [for him] but are trustworthy, give the following oath: ‘that he makes his claim against that estate according to folk-right, since his cattle went up there’.

If that man [the local] says that [the owner of the cattle] unjustly follows the trail, then this [man] who owns the cattle must conduct [them both back] to the bank; and there as one of six unselected [oath-takers], who are trustworthy, give an oath there that he asserts within [the terms of] customary law that his cattle went there.
div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; B reads ‘ah trod’ and ‘ofer’; Liebermann prints ‘[o]ð’ and supplies ‘orf’ from Ld and the Quadripartitus. B and Ld read ‘ahtrodað’, which the Quadripartitus also understands as a verb derived from ‘trod’. Liebermann compares II As 9.

note.seg: ahtrodað to s. BLd; auch Quadr. versteht 3. Sing. Praes. eines von trod abgeleiteten Verbs
ahtrodað to s. BLd; Quadr. too takes it as the 3rd sing. pres. of a verb derived from trod

Thorpe erkannte die Überlieferung als korrupt; Schmids Besserung nimmt Toller s. v. trod zweifelnd an. Trennt man aber ah nicht, so fehlt ein Objekt zu lædan. Und ein Verb, von dem *atrodað (wenn h blosse Verschreibung wäre) herkäme, fehlt; atreddan heisst ‘erforschen’ und trodden (12. Jh.) ‘nachspüren’; an deren eines dachte Q

Thorpe recognized the transmitted text as corrupt; Schmid’s emendation is accepted, with doubt, by Toller s. v. trod. But if ah is not separated off, lædan lacks an object. And there is no verb from which *atrodað (if h were a mere slip of the pen) could derive; atreddan means ‘to search out’ and trodden (12th cent.) ‘to track’; Q was thinking of one of these
Im Ggs. zum Auswahleid (s. d. Gl 4. 6), der 6, 2{2a} vorkommt. Vgl. Gl Klageeid 4a; Eidesformeln 4 B I
